answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake tied to one verifiable identity: an agent must lock funds before it can vote or claim rewards, and the stake is slashed if duplicate identities are proven. Forging a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand stakes, like trying to grow a vine from every cutting without soil. A falcon-eyed audit may miss one fake, but a ferrous, auditable bond makes mass forgery unprofitable rather than merely forbidden.
